title: The impact of package selection and versioning on single-cell RNA-seq analysis

links.name: Cell Systems
links.summary: Single-cell RNA-seq workflows shape biological interpretation, so reproducible package behavior matters when analyses pass through many algorithmic steps. Widely used tools are often treated as interchangeable, but Seurat/Scanpy choices and version changes can alter outputs from feature selection through differential expression. By comparing package and version effects across the standard pipeline, the article establishes metrics for assessing those differences.

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: Single-cell RNA-seq analyses increasingly depend on shared software defaults, making package behavior a reproducibility issue rather than a cosmetic implementation detail. The challenge is that Seurat, Scanpy, Cell Ranger, and their versions can differ even when workflows appear similar. Quantifying package, version, and downsampling effects provides methods for comparing pipeline steps from filtering to differential expression.

summary: Single-cell RNA-seq workflows shape biological interpretation, so reproducible package behavior matters when analyses pass through many algorithmic steps. title: Systematic cell-type resolved transcriptomes of 8 tissues in 8 lab and wild-derived mouse strains capture global and local expression variation

links.name: Cell Genomics
links.summary: Genetic diversity shapes physiology through cell-type-specific programs, so resolving expression variation at cellular resolution is essential for connecting genotype to disease. Bulk tissue profiles and limited strain panels can obscure where strain and sex effects concentrate. The Cell Genomics resource maps eight Collaborative Cross founder strains across eight tissue groups, showing that genotype-driven and disease-relevant signatures localize to particular cell types.

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: Genetic background influences disease and trait variation, but its cellular basis is difficult to resolve without coordinated multi-tissue data. Existing mouse resources often lack matched strain, sex, tissue, and cell-type coverage at single-nucleus scale. The 8-cube dataset profiles eight founder strains across eight tissues and shows that strain and sex effects concentrate in specific cell types and disease-associated states.

title: Verifying LLM-extracted text with token alignment

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: LLMs can extract useful text from documents, but scientific reuse requires knowing whether an extracted passage is actually supported by the source. Verification is difficult when answers combine non-contiguous phrases or when token boundaries do not match words. Ordered subword alignment benchmarks and the taln implementation demonstrate that LLM-extracted text can be checked deterministically against source documents without relying on semantic judgment.

title: Science should be machine-readable

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: Scientific papers contain results that machines could help audit and compare, but prose-first publication leaves those claims difficult to recover reliably after the fact. The gap is a lack of structured claims, evidence, and evaluations produced at publication scale. OpenEval demonstrates a machine-automated pipeline over the full eLife corpus and argues that machine-readable science should be generated during publication rather than reconstructed later.

title: Long-read sequencing transcriptome quantification with lr-kallisto

links.name: PLOS Computational Biology
links.summary: Long-read RNA sequencing can clarify transcript isoforms, but transcriptome-scale quantification still needs methods that are both accurate and computationally efficient. Existing long-read tools can be slower or more memory intensive, and enrichment strategies such as exome capture need quantitative evaluation. lr-kallisto adapts kallisto pseudoalignment for long reads and demonstrates accurate ONT quantification, improved performance with exome capture, and lower runtime and memory use.

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: Long-read RNA sequencing offers isoform-level information, but routine transcript quantification depends on methods that scale without sacrificing accuracy. The challenge is extending fast pseudoalignment ideas from short-read kallisto to noisy long-read data across technologies and simulations. lr-kallisto adapts kallisto for long reads and demonstrates accurate, efficient quantification on ONT data, other long-read platforms, and simulated benchmarks.

summary: Long-read RNA sequencing can clarify transcript isoforms, but transcriptome-scale quantification still needs methods that are both accurate and computationally efficient. title: Determining gene specificity from multivariate single-cell RNA sequencing data

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: Single-cell atlases can reveal where genes are specific, but marker interpretation becomes complicated when variation spans cell types, tissues, strains, and individuals. Existing specificity measures do not always satisfy clear information-theoretic properties or handle multivariate context. ember introduces entropy-based metrics for gene specificity and applies them to mouse and human datasets, revealing context-dependent markers, housekeeping genes, strain effects, and PBMC variation localized to classical monocytes.

title: Single-Nucleus Analysis of Human White Adipose Tissue Reveals Adipocyte Subsets with Distinct Metabolic Profiles

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: Human white adipose tissue contributes to metabolic disease, but depot-level measurements can miss functionally distinct adipocyte states. The challenge is resolving adipocyte heterogeneity and linking those states to obesity, glycemia, diabetes, and regulators of adipogenesis. Single-nucleus profiling identifies ADIPOMAThi and ADIPOMATlo adipocytes with distinct metabolic profiles and implicates TSHZ3 as an in vivo regulator of adipose tissue development.

title: Comparative survey-based study of noninvasive saliva collection devices

links.name: Journal of Medical Devices
links.summary: Saliva diagnostics matter because whole saliva can be collected noninvasively and can support applications ranging from infectious disease testing to biomarker monitoring. Yet collection protocols are not standardized, and device usability, leakage, and collection efficiency can affect sample quality and user safety. By comparing five representative devices in 60 adults, the work identifies tradeoffs across metrics and motivates better standardized, user-friendly saliva collection designs.

links.name: medRxiv
links.summary: Saliva-based testing is valuable because it can make diagnostic sampling less invasive and easier to deploy at scale. The practical challenge is that swabs, funnels, and passive drool devices differ in efficiency, readability, leakage, and user burden, leaving collection protocols unstandardized. This preprint compares five devices with timed collection, reading-rate normalization, surveys, and stimulated-flow measurements to define design criteria for safer and easier saliva collection.

title: kallisto, bustools and kb-python for quantifying bulk, single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq

links.name: Nature Protocols
links.summary: RNA-seq preprocessing is central to turning sequencing reads into expression measurements for bulk tissues, single cells, and single nuclei. The challenge is that mapping, barcode correction, UMI handling, reference construction, and assay-specific settings require multiple coordinated steps. The protocol gives a reproducible kallisto, bustools, and kb-python workflow that reduces preprocessing to reference generation and quantification while supporting standard, nascent-and-cDNA, bulk, single-cell, and single-nucleus analyses.

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: RNA-seq assays matter because they quantify RNA species across bulk samples, individual cells, and nuclei. The preprocessing gap is that raw FASTQs, genome references, assay chemistries, barcodes, UMIs, and nascent transcript signals otherwise require many coordinated tool invocations and choices. This protocol describes how kallisto, bustools, and kb-python create efficient two-step workflows with standard and nascent/coding-DNA references, count matrices, bulk abundance outputs, and downstream interoperability.

summary: RNA-seq preprocessing is central to turning sequencing reads into expression measurements for bulk tissues, single cells, and single nuclei. title: Deciphering the impact of genomic variation on function

links.name: Nature
links.summary: Human genomic variation is a route to understanding biology, disease risk, diagnosis, and therapy. The central difficulty is that variant effects depend on molecular function, cell type, context, population, and networks, making comprehensive experimental mapping impossible by brute force. The IGVF Consortium establishes a coordinated map-perturb-predict program that will combine single-cell maps, large-scale perturbations, predictive models, benchmarks, and an open catalog of variant effects.

versions.title: The impact of genomic variation on function (IGVF) consortium
versions.name: arXiv
versions.summary: Human genetics has linked vast numbers of variants to traits and disease, making variant-to-function interpretation essential for precision medicine. The challenge is scale and context: most variants lack perturbation data, disease associations contain many candidates, and effects can depend on cell type, population, and molecular networks. The IGVF Consortium proposes a coordinated map-perturb-predict framework, shared standards, and open data resources to build variant-effect maps across cell types and populations.

title: A machine-readable specification for genomics assays

links.name: Bioinformatics
links.summary: Accurate preprocessing of genomics reads depends on knowing how biological and technical sequences are arranged in each library. The gap is that assay-specific scripts, divergent parameters, and non-machine-readable library descriptions make uniform processing, comparison, and reanalysis difficult. Seqspec contributes a YAML-based specification and command-line tool for annotating library regions, validating specifications, and generating tool-compatible preprocessing inputs for standardized genomics workflows.

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: Genomics assays are only reusable and comparable when the structure of their sequenced reads is explicit. The obstacle is that complex library designs, assay-specific scripts, and existing formats leave barcodes, UMIs, biological inserts, and platform details under-specified for automated preprocessing. Seqspec addresses this by defining a human- and machine-readable YAML specification plus tooling that indexes read regions and emits preprocessing strings for kallisto bustools, simpleaf/alevin-fry, and STARsolo.

title: Algorithms for a Commons Cell Atlas

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: Cell atlases are valuable because they organize single-cell datasets into reference maps of tissues, cell types, and marker genes. Current atlas projects remain difficult to update or jointly analyze because preprocessing is inconsistent, marker curation is manual, and compatible reanalysis tools are limited. The work introduces mx, ec, cellatlas, and Commons Cell Atlas infrastructure for automated filtering, normalization, cell-type assignment, marker updating, and reproducible atlas construction.

title: A human commons cell atlas reveals cell type specificity for OAS1 isoforms

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: OAS1 isoforms matter because innate antiviral protection depends on which transcripts are present in the cell types a virus infects. Existing cell atlases largely report gene-level counts, making isoform-specific and dynamically reprocessable questions difficult. By building a 2.9-million-cell Human Commons Cell Atlas from raw FASTQs and reprocessing it at isoform resolution, the work identifies testis-specific OAS1-p44b expression in spermatogenesis cells and demonstrates a flexible atlas model for custom analyses.

title: Quantifying orthogonal barcodes for sequence census assays

links.name: Bioinformatics Advances
links.summary: Multimodal and perturbation assays increasingly depend on short orthogonal barcodes to connect sequencing reads with proteins, samples, guides, and other features. Assay-specific tools and barcode design failures can introduce ambiguous assignment, runtime costs, and inconsistent processing across technologies. kITE uses kallisto/bustools mismatch-index pseudoalignment to quantify diverse barcode assays efficiently, and qcbc adds design diagnostics that expose shared subsequences, homopolymers, distance issues, and other error modes.

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: Barcode-based multimodal assays broaden what can be measured in single cells, but short feature barcodes and assay-specific workflows make quantification fragile and difficult to standardize. kITE builds a mismatched kallisto index to pseudoalign and error-collapse barcode reads across feature barcoding, sample hashing, and perturbation assays. The preprint also introduces qcbc to diagnose barcode designs and simulations showing how shared subsequences and low diversity lead to ambiguous assignments.

title: Universal preprocessing of single-cell genomics data

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: Large single-cell atlases depend on comparing datasets generated by many assays, so preprocessing must be consistent before biological interpretation begins. Existing workflows are often assay-specific, while read structures, barcode correction, and UMI/read counting differ across RNA, ATAC, protein, tags, and spatial modalities. cellatlas uses machine-readable seqspec files to configure kb-python, kallisto/bustools, kITE, and snATAK, demonstrating uniform preprocessing across nine datasets and enabling modality and technology comparisons.

title: Voyager: exploratory single-cell genomics data analysis with geospatial statistics

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: Spatial organization is central to tissue function, and spatial omics needs exploratory tools that can reason directly over geometry, neighborhoods, and autocorrelation. Existing single-cell frameworks only partially incorporate the geospatial ESDA tradition and can also produce language-dependent results across R and Python implementations. Voyager combines SpatialFeatureExperiment geometry support, scalable univariate/bivariate/multivariate ESDA, reproducible tutorials, and compatibility-tested R/Python implementations to reveal signals such as library-size biology and negative spatial autocorrelation.

title: Characterization of spatial homogeneous regions in tissues with concordex

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: Single-cell RNA-seq analyses often use labels, clusters, and integration assessments derived from kNN graphs, but two-dimensional embeddings can distort the graph while inviting visual overinterpretation. The gap is a direct, quantitative way to test whether categorical labels agree with local neighborhoods without depending on UMAP aesthetics or hyperparameters. CONCORDEX computes same-label and different-label neighbor fractions, compares concordance with random labelings, and shows strong agreement with simulated assignment accuracy while exposing misleading integration and cluster views.

versions.title: Characterization of spatial homogeneous regions in tissues with concordex
versions.name: bioRxiv v3
versions.summary: Spatial transcriptomics can reveal tissue organization, but spatially variable gene calls are hard to interpret when cell-type composition and location are entangled. Existing domain methods may identify regions without separating cell-type effects from spatial effects or their interactions. concordex defines spatial homogeneous regions from kNN neighborhood composition, works with discrete or continuous labels across SRT platforms, and pairs those regions with a negative-binomial GLM to identify subtle spatial and cell-type interaction patterns.

versions.title: Quantitative assessment of single-cell RNA-seq clustering with CONCORDEX
versions.name: bioRxiv v2
versions.summary: Spatial transcriptomics aims to organize cells into tissue regions whose composition reflects biology rather than plotting artifacts. Existing spatial-domain methods often rely on gene expression smoothing or neural networks, leaving the definition of a region ambiguous and sometimes conflating cell type with tissue domain. concordex builds neighborhood consolidation matrices on kNN graphs to identify spatial homogeneous regions across liver, cerebellum, and simulations, while also quantifying cluster and integration relationships in non-spatial transcriptomics.

title: Assessing the multimodal tradeoff

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: Multimodal single-cell assays can connect transcription, chromatin accessibility, and other measurements in the same cells, but added modalities can reduce data quality, raise costs, and complicate cross-platform comparison. The challenge is that ATAC and RNA components often use different preprocessing software and read structures, which can add computational variability before tradeoffs are measured. snATAK provides a uniform kallisto/bustools-based preprocessing workflow for chromatin assays, validates concordance with Cell Ranger while running faster, and uses uniform processing to quantify Multiome, SHARE-seqV2, ISSAAC-seq, and allele-concordance tradeoffs.

title: Metadata retrieval from sequence databases with ffq

links.name: Bioinformatics
links.summary: Public sequencing archives are increasingly reused for new analyses, making metadata retrieval and raw-data link discovery part of practical genomics work. Existing tools tend to cover limited repositories, and user-submitted metadata remains uneven and difficult to standardize. ffq exploits common database hierarchies and public APIs to return accession- or DOI-derived metadata and data links as JSON, enabling lightweight command-line parsing and streamwise downstream processing.

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: Reusable public sequencing data depends on accurate metadata, but researchers must query multiple repositories with inconsistent interfaces and incomplete user submissions. The initial ffq release identifies shared hierarchical structures across SRA, GEO, ENA, DDBJ GEA, and ENCODE, while limiting the tool to metadata and link retrieval. It returns JSON from accession or DOI queries through public APIs, integrates with command-line parsers, and argues that better machine-readable upload standards remain necessary.

title: Pseudoalignment facilitates assignment of error-prone Ultima Genomics reads

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: Lower-cost sequencing could expand single-cell genomics and clinical sequencing, but new platforms must preserve gene-level accuracy as well as throughput. Ultima Genomics reads in this PBMC comparison showed elevated homopolymer-associated errors that reduced standard alignment for genes such as TMSB4X. Pseudoalignment in kallisto-bustools recovered substantially more error-prone reads than alignment, while still leaving residual bias when error rates were very high.

title: Normalization for sampled count data

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: Single-cell RNA-seq normalization is a first step that shapes PCA, clustering, differential expression, and marker visualization. The original 2022 preprint identifies a practical tradeoff: popular methods stabilize variance, normalize depth, or preserve monotonicity, but often not all three at once. It benchmarks hundreds of datasets and introduces PFlog1pPF as a sparse, monotonic heuristic that adds a second proportional-fitting step to improve depth normalization while retaining useful variance behavior.

versions.title: Normalization for sampled count data
versions.name: bioRxiv v4
versions.summary: Reliable genomics count analysis depends on normalization that preserves biological structure while removing technical effects. Common single-cell workflows still leave residual depth structure, alter within-cell ranks, or impose dense-memory costs. The 2026 v4 formulation defines PFlog as an Anscombe-calibrated shifted centered-log-ratio transform, proves it uniquely satisfies the desired equivariant criteria, and benchmarks it across hundreds of datasets with improved depth, rank, and geometry behavior.

versions.title: Depth normalization for single-cell genomics count data
versions.name: bioRxiv v3
versions.summary: Single-cell analyses rely on normalization before PCA, clustering, and marker discovery, so normalization errors can propagate into biological interpretation. The June 10 version argues that widely used log-normalized and residual-based workflows incompletely balance variance stabilization, depth normalization, and monotonicity. It formalizes PFlog1pPF as a shifted centered-log-ratio transform and shows improved benchmark, downsampling, and feature-panel stability across large single-cell datasets.

versions.title: Depth normalization for single-cell genomics count data
versions.name: bioRxiv v2
versions.summary: Single-cell count normalization matters because downstream neighborhood graphs and marker rankings are sensitive to depth and feature-panel choices. The June 7 version frames the unresolved gap as jointly achieving variance stabilization, depth normalization, and monotonicity without sacrificing sparse workflows. It proposes PFlog1pPF and shows stronger downsampling robustness, reduced feature-panel dependence, and better overall tradeoffs than common log1pPF and residual-based methods.

title: A transcriptomic and epigenomic cell atlas of the mouse primary motor cortex

links.name: Nature
links.summary: Brain cell atlases are useful only when molecularly defined types are reproducible across assays and interpretable in anatomical context. Mouse primary motor cortex had fragmented transcriptomic and epigenomic evidence, including uncertainty about fine cell-type resolution and L4-like excitatory neurons. The atlas integrates more than 500,000 cells across RNA, DNA methylation, and chromatin-accessibility modalities, validates a reproducible taxonomy, links regulatory elements to cell types, and revises the view of MOp as strictly agranular.

title: A multimodal cell census and atlas of the mammalian primary motor cortex

links.name: Nature
links.summary: Understanding motor cortex organization requires a reference that connects molecular cell identities to anatomy, physiology, projections, spatial location, and species conservation. Before BICCN integration, these modalities were often measured in separate studies, leaving correspondence among cell-type definitions uncertain. The atlas combines coordinated mouse, marmoset, and human datasets into a conserved hierarchical taxonomy and registers multimodal phenotypes, wiring, genetic tools, and gene-regulatory features into a shared primary motor cortex framework.

title: Isoform cell-type specificity in the mouse primary motor cortex

links.name: Nature
links.summary: Isoform regulation is central to neuronal differentiation and disease, but most single-cell brain atlases collapse transcripts to gene-level counts. That gene-level view can miss cell-type-specific isoform switches and spatial patterns that matter for interpreting neuronal diversity. By linking SMART-seq isoform quantification with 10x cell-type assignments and MERFISH spatial data, the study builds a mouse MOp isoform atlas and identifies isoform markers, shifts, and regulatory programs hidden from gene-level analysis.

title: Massively scaled-up testing for SARS-CoV-2 RNA via next-generation sequencing of pooled and barcoded nasal and saliva samples

links.name: Nature Biomedical Engineering
links.summary: Frequent asymptomatic testing can suppress viral transmission, but RT-qPCR capacity, extraction workflows, and cost limited population-scale SARS-CoV-2 screening. SwabSeq addresses that bottleneck by combining sample barcodes, end-point RT-PCR, and synthetic RNA standards so pooled sequencing can call thousands of nasal or saliva specimens without RNA extraction. Clinical validation and deployment showed qPCR-comparable performance, extraction-free workflows, and more than 80,000 returned tests with sub-24-hour turnaround.

title: Low-cost, scalable, and automated fluid sampling for fluidics applications

links.name: HardwareX
links.summary: Automated fraction collection is useful for microfluidics and chromatography, but commercial systems can be costly, bulky, and difficult to customize. Colosseum addresses this access gap with an open-source, 3D-printed, single-motor fraction collector that can be assembled cheaply from off-the-shelf parts. Bench tests and gradient collections show accurate, scalable sampling across common fluidics applications.

title: Modular, efficient and constant-memory single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing

links.name: Nature Biotechnology
links.summary: Single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing determines whether large assays can be analyzed accurately and affordably. Growing datasets expose bottlenecks in memory, speed, and workflow flexibility, especially when users need downstream analyses such as RNA velocity. The kallisto-bustools workflow uses BUS-based modular preprocessing to achieve near-optimal speed, constant memory, Cell Ranger-concordant counts, and scalable RNA velocity analysis.

title: Benchmarking of lightweight-mapping based single-cell RNA-seq pre-processing

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: Single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing is a prerequisite for interpreting growing cellular datasets, so users need tools that are both reproducible and computationally practical. The challenge is deciding whether competing lightweight-mapping workflows differ meaningfully in output, usability, speed, or memory. A comparison across 20 datasets finds kallisto-bustools and Salmon-Alevin-fry produce nearly identical downstream results, while Salmon-Alevin-fry is slower, more memory-intensive, and more expensive to run.

title: Normalization of single-cell RNA-seq counts by log (x+ 1) or log (1+ x)

links.name: Bioinformatics
links.summary: Single-cell atlases are often used to reason about clinically important genes, but sparse counts make naive comparisons fragile. For low-abundance targets such as ACE2, filtering to nonzero cells and applying log1p transformations can create misleading impressions of expression. These examples clarify the statistical interpretation of positive-cell fractions and warn that common normalization choices can distort comparative estimates when their limitations are ignored.

title: Reliable and accurate diagnostics from highly multiplexed sequencing assays

links.name: Nature Scientific Reports
links.summary: Scalable infectious-disease testing depends on software that can turn multiplexed sequencing reads into reliable clinical calls. Sequencing-based SARS-CoV-2 assays promise high throughput, but they require transparent, portable, statistically sound analysis pipelines. The kallisto-bustools HMSA workflow processes SwabSeq and related assays quickly, validates sample classification and viral-load estimation, and generalizes to multiple diagnostic sequencing designs.

title: Markedly heterogeneous COVID-19 testing plans among US colleges and universities

links.name: MedRxiv
links.summary: Safe campus reopening during COVID-19 depended on testing plans that could identify infections before outbreaks spread. U.S. colleges faced conflicting guidance, uneven resources, and opaque public communication, producing wide variation in whether and how communities would be screened. A survey of more than 500 institutions documents heterogeneous testing strategies, divergence from emerging best practices for frequent testing, and equity concerns tied to institutional resources and worker access.

title: Decrease in ACE2 mRNA expression in aged mouse lung

links.name: bioRxiv
links.summary: Understanding why COVID-19 severity rises with age requires evidence about host factors such as ACE2 in relevant tissues. Available human data were limited, and speculation about age-dependent ACE2 expression needed cell-type-resolved analysis. Analysis of young and old mouse lung single-cell and bulk RNA-seq finds reduced ACE2 mRNA with age, localized partly to ciliated-cell expression and abundance changes, while TMPRSS2 did not show the same pattern.

title: Principles of open source bioinstrumentation applied to the poseidon syringe pump system

links.name: Nature Scientific Reports
links.summary: Open bioinstrumentation can lower costs and let laboratories adapt hardware to fast-changing biological experiments. Adoption is limited when designs are hard to build, unsafe, poorly documented, or insufficiently benchmarked. The Poseidon syringe pump and microscope system demonstrates a sub-$400 open-source microfluidics platform and uses it to articulate seven design principles for functional, robust, safe, simple, modular, benchmarked, and documented instruments.

links.name: Correction

versions.name: bioRxiv
versions.summary: Accessible bioinstrumentation can help laboratories run and modify microfluidic experiments without depending on rigid commercial systems. The main challenge is not just cost, but whether open designs are easy to adopt, adapt, validate, and document. A low-cost Poseidon syringe pump and microscope system distills six design principles for open-source bioinstrumentation, supported by droplet-generation benchmarking against a commercial system.

title: Thermo-electrochemical generator: energy harvesting & thermoregulation for liquid cooling applications

links.name: Sustainable Energy & Fuels
links.summary: Recovering low-grade waste heat matters because data centers and other liquid-cooled systems spend substantial energy removing heat that is otherwise unused. Conventional thermoelectric approaches face material, geometry, and transport limitations, especially at low temperatures. The flow thermo-electrochemical cell couples liquid cooling with redox-based energy harvesting, demonstrating convective cooling, measurable power output, and a path toward temperature monitoring and recycled power in liquid-cooled infrastructure.
